questions.q: But-2-yne is treated with one mole of H₂ over Lindlar catalyst. The product is:
questions.explain: Both hydrogens are delivered from the palladium surface to the same face of the triple bond (syn addition), giving the cis alkene; the poisoned catalyst cannot reduce it further to butane.

questions.q: Which reagent converts dec-5-yne into trans-dec-5-ene?
questions.explain: Sodium in liquid ammonia adds electrons and protons one at a time and gives the trans alkene. Lindlar and P-2 both give the cis alkene, and unpoisoned Pd/C goes all the way to the alkane.

questions.q: Which statement about Lindlar catalyst is INCORRECT?
options: It is palladium on CaCO₃ (or BaSO₄) poisoned with lead acetate and quinoline
Its active metal is nickel, deposited on barium sulphate
It adds hydrogen to an alkyne by syn addition
It does not reduce the alkene that forms
questions.explain: The metal in Lindlar catalyst is palladium. Nickel appears only in the separate P-2 catalyst (nickel boride), a common mix-up.

questions.q: Hept-1-en-6-yne takes up exactly one mole of H₂ over Lindlar catalyst. The product is:
questions.explain: Lindlar catalyst reduces only the C≡C of an enyne and leaves the isolated C=C untouched, so the terminal alkyne becomes a second terminal alkene.
